First impressions and movement in schizophrenia

Statistical analysis pipeline

Statistical analysis report

2026-10-01

1 Introduction

This notebook reports the statistical analysis of first impressions formed about individuals with schizophrenia (SZ) and matched healthy controls (P), and the relationship between these impressions and the quantity of body movement (QoM) of the hands and of the head, extracted from short video stimuli.

The movement analysis uses four directional quantity-of-motion (QoM) features, extracted at the stimulus level:

  • move_hands_horizontal_qom_rate — hand movement, horizontal (per second);
  • move_hands_vertical_qom_rate — hand movement, vertical (per second);
  • move_head_horizontal_qom_rate — head movement, horizontal (per second);
  • move_head_vertical_qom_rate — head movement, vertical (per second).

These are first correlated, then reduced to a single overall movement component by PCA, which is used in the group and impression analyses.

This is the last step of the pipeline. Results are organised by hypothesis under results/: descriptive/ (purely descriptive tables, no hypothesis test), H1/ (group -> impression), H2/ (group -> movement), H3/ (movement -> impression), H4/ (group and movement jointly), and supplementary/ (scale reliability, the movement PCA construction, and exploratory/symptom correlations).

2 Materials and methods

2.1 Software

R.version.string
## [1] "R version 4.5.2 (2025-10-31 ucrt)"

Analyses were performed in R with the following packages: lme4, lmerTest, emmeans, performance, effectsize, psych, car, flextable, gt, ggplot2, patchwork. The full session information is reported at the end of this document.

2.2 Statistical analyses

Alpha level. All inferential tests used a two-sided α = 0.05 unless otherwise specified.

Descriptive statistics. Continuous variables are summarised as mean (SD) when approximately normally distributed and as median [Q1, Q3] otherwise. Sample sizes (N) are reported for every analysis. Standard deviations (not standard errors) are used to convey variability.

Group comparisons (P vs. SZ) at the stimulus level. For each continuous variable, the test was selected automatically: (i) Shapiro–Wilk per group tested normality and Levene’s test tested homogeneity of variances; (ii) when both assumptions held, an independent-samples Student t-test was used; (iii) when variances differed, Welch’s t-test; (iv) when normality failed, the Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Effect sizes are Cohen’s d for t-tests and the rank-biserial correlation for Wilcoxon tests, each with a 95 % CI.

Linear mixed models (LMM). For analyses on the evaluation-level data (one row per observer × video), LMMs were fitted with lmerTest using restricted maximum likelihood (REML). Random intercepts were specified for observer and for video stimulus, outcome ~ predictor(s) + (1 | obs_id) + (1 | vid). Denominator degrees of freedom and p-values were obtained via Satterthwaite’s approximation. For every LMM we report (a) the fixed-effect estimates with 95 % CI, (b) the marginal R² (variance explained by the fixed effects) and conditional R² (fixed + random effects) following Nakagawa & Schielzeth, and (c) an explicit partition of the random variance: the variance component and the proportion of the residual (unexplained) variance attributable to each random intercept (observer, video) and to the residual, together with the intraclass correlation (ICC = proportion of residual variance captured by the random intercepts). The additional variance accounted for by the random structure beyond the fixed effects is summarised by conditional R² − marginal R². For the two-group models (total score and each item) a standardised mean-difference effect size (Cohen’s d, SZ − P) is additionally obtained from the estimated marginal means with emmeans::eff_size(). Model assumptions (normality of residuals, homoscedasticity, normality of the random-effect BLUPs, singularity and convergence) were checked numerically and visually with performance::check_model().

Aggregating the movement features. The four directional QoM features (hands and head × horizontal and vertical) were first inter-correlated at the stimulus level (Pearson’s r when all features were approximately normal by Shapiro-Wilk, otherwise Spearman’s ρ). Given their strong inter-correlations, they were reduced by a principal component analysis on the z-standardised features. Sampling adequacy was checked (Kaiser-Meyer- Olkin measure; Bartlett’s test of sphericity); the number of components was determined by the Kaiser criterion (eigenvalue > 1) and parallel analysis, and a varimax (orthogonal) rotation was applied when more than one component was retained (no effect for a single component). Eigenvalues, communalities and a scree plot are reported. The dominant component — oriented so that higher scores indicate more movement and rescaled to unit SD — was used as a single overall body movement score in the subsequent analyses.

Group difference in movement. The group difference in overall body movement was tested on this aggregate score at the stimulus level, with the test auto-selected from normality and variance-homogeneity checks and reported with its effect size.

Group and movement jointly. The first-impression total-score model was then re-fitted with both diagnostic group and overall movement as fixed effects. This estimates the movement effect adjusting for group and quantifies the attenuation of the group difference once movement is accounted for (a mediation-style comparison, reported descriptively). Because group and movement are correlated at the stimulus level, their collinearity (VIF) is reported alongside.

Robustness. Because several impression models showed mild heteroscedasticity, the principal fixed effects were re-estimated with a non-parametric cluster bootstrap (resampling whole video stimuli with replacement), and compared with the model-based estimates as a sensitivity analysis. The bootstrap is valid for the crossed observer × video random structure, for which sandwich-type cluster-robust estimators are not defined.

Correlations. Spearman’s ρ was used throughout (no normality requirement, robust to the small SZ sample), with 95 % CIs from Fisher’s z transformation. Correlations among clinical variables are flagged as exploratory (post-hoc) per SAMPL.

Multiple comparisons. When several tests addressed one family of hypotheses, Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) false-discovery-rate correction was applied and the adjusted p-values are reported alongside the raw values (impression items: family of ten items; exploratory correlations: family of features within each clinical variable).

Missing data. No imputation was performed; each test uses complete cases on the variables involved, and sample sizes are reported per analysis.

# Colours, labels, fmt_*() helpers, theme_plos(), plos_table(), save_table()
# and save_figure() - the formatting/journal-style layer, kept separate so it
# can be tweaked without touching the analyses below.
source("style_helpers.R")
source("stat_helpers.R")

# ---- Movement variables (only the two total-QoM features) ------------------
MOVEMENT_VARS <- c(
  "move_hands_horizontal_qom_rate",  # hand movement, horizontal (QoM rate)
  "move_hands_vertical_qom_rate",    # hand movement, vertical (QoM rate)
  "move_head_horizontal_qom_rate",   # head movement, horizontal (QoM rate)
  "move_head_vertical_qom_rate"      # head movement, vertical (QoM rate)
)

IMPRESSION_ITEMS <- c(
  "imp_sympathique", "imp_bizarre_inversed", "imp_intelligente",
  "imp_appreciable", "imp_confiance", "imp_dominante",
  "imp_conversation", "imp_temps", "imp_voisin", "imp_assis"
)

ALPHA_LEVEL <- 0.05

# ---- Input path (processed data from 02_merge_data.Rmd) ------------------
PATH_DATA_PROC <- "../../data/merged"

# ---- Output paths: results organised by hypothesis --------------------------
RESULTS_DIR           <- "../../results"
RESULTS_DESCRIPTIVE   <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "descriptive")
RESULTS_H1             <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "H1")   # group -> impression
RESULTS_H2             <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "H2")   # group -> movement
RESULTS_H3             <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "H3")   # movement -> impression
RESULTS_H4             <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "H4")   # group + movement jointly
RESULTS_SUPPLEMENTARY <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "supplementary")

for (p in c(RESULTS_DESCRIPTIVE, RESULTS_H1, RESULTS_H2, RESULTS_H3, RESULTS_H4,
            RESULTS_SUPPLEMENTARY)) {
  dir.create(p, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

3.2 Load processed data

Reads the three tables produced by 02_prepare_data.Rmd (data/questionnaire_and_merged/02_data_*.csv). No merging happens here.

data_complete  <- read_csv(file.path(PATH_DATA_PROC, "data_complete.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
data_stimuli   <- read_csv(file.path(PATH_DATA_PROC, "data_stimuli.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
data_observers <- read_csv(file.path(PATH_DATA_PROC, "data_observers.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)

data_complete$stim_group <- factor(data_complete$stim_group, levels = c("P", "SZ"))
data_stimuli$stim_group  <- factor(data_stimuli$stim_group,  levels = c("P", "SZ"))

message(sprintf("data_complete : %d rows / data_stimuli : %d rows / data_observers : %d rows",
                nrow(data_complete), nrow(data_stimuli), nrow(data_observers)))
## data_complete : 910 rows / data_stimuli : 40 rows / data_observers : 91 rows

4 Results

4.1 Reliability of the first-impression scale

Purpose. Estimate the internal consistency of the 10 first-impression items used to compute the total impression score.

Items used. imp_bizarre_inversed is the recoded (reverse) version of imp_bizarre; only the inverted version is included in the score and in the reliability analysis.

alpha_obj <- psych::alpha(
  data_complete[, IMPRESSION_ITEMS, drop = FALSE],
  check.keys = FALSE,
  warnings = FALSE
)
## Number of categories should be increased  in order to count frequencies.
alpha_summary <- tibble(
  `N items` = length(IMPRESSION_ITEMS),
  `N observations` = sum(complete.cases(
    data_complete[, IMPRESSION_ITEMS]
  )),
  `Cronbach's α` = alpha_obj$total$raw_alpha
)

ft_alpha <- alpha_summary |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ fmt_num(.x, 3))) |>
  plos_table(
    title = "Internal consistency of the 10-item first-impression scale.",
    footnote = paste0(
      "Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's α. ",
      "imp_bizarre_inversed is the reverse-scored version of imp_bizarre."
    )
  )

4.2 Characteristics of stimulus participants

Purpose. Describe and compare the two stimulus groups (P vs. SZ) on demographic and general cognitive variables.

Method. Each continuous variable was tested with auto_group_test(), which selects between Student’s t-test, Welch’s t-test, and the Wilcoxon rank-sum test on the basis of Shapiro–Wilk and Levene tests. Gender is reported as count and column percentage; group differences in gender are tested with Pearson’s χ² (or Fisher’s exact when expected counts are < 5).

vars_stim_continu <- c("stim_age", "stim_education",
                       "stim_BDI_II", "stim_fNART_errors", "stim_MOCA")

# --- Continuous variables: auto-test ----------------------------------------
stim_tests <- auto_group_test_multi(data_stimuli, vars_stim_continu,
                                    group_var = "stim_group",
                                    bh_correction = FALSE)

# --- Gender (chi-square / Fisher) -------------------------------------------
gender_tab <- table(data_stimuli$stim_gender, data_stimuli$stim_group)
gender_test <- if (any(chisq.test(gender_tab)$expected < 5)) {
  res <- fisher.test(gender_tab)
  list(name = "Fisher's exact", stat = NA_real_,
       df = NA_real_, p = res$p.value, es = NA, lo = NA, hi = NA)
} else {
  res <- chisq.test(gender_tab)
  v   <- effectsize::cramers_v(gender_tab)
  list(name = "χ²", stat = unname(res$statistic), df = unname(res$parameter),
       p = res$p.value, es = v$Cramers_v_adjusted,
       lo = v$CI_low, hi = v$CI_high)
}

# --- Build the publication table --------------------------------------------
n_p  <- sum(data_stimuli$stim_group == "P",  na.rm = TRUE)
n_sz <- sum(data_stimuli$stim_group == "SZ", na.rm = TRUE)

gender_rows <- data_stimuli |>
  count(stim_group, stim_gender) |>
  group_by(stim_group) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, pct)) |>
  select(stim_group, stim_gender, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = stim_group, values_from = cell)

gender_first_row <- tibble(
  Variable    = paste0("Gender, n (%)"),
  P_value     = gender_rows[[2]][1],
  SZ_value    = gender_rows[[3]][1],
  Test        = gender_test$name,
  Statistic   = if (!is.na(gender_test$stat))
                  sprintf("%s%s",
                          fmt_num(gender_test$stat, 2),
                          ifelse(is.na(gender_test$df), "",
                                 sprintf(" (df = %d)", gender_test$df)))
                else "—",
  p           = fmt_p(gender_test$p),
  `Effect size (95% CI)` = if (!is.na(gender_test$es))
    sprintf("V = %s %s", fmt_num(gender_test$es, 2),
            fmt_ci(gender_test$lo, gender_test$hi, 2))
    else "—"
)

continu_rows <- stim_tests |>
  mutate(
    Variable = paste0(pretty_label(outcome), ", mean (SD)"),
    P_value  = fmt_msd(mean_g1, sd_g1, 2),
    SZ_value = fmt_msd(mean_g2, sd_g2, 2),
    Test     = test,
    Statistic = ifelse(is.na(df),
                       fmt_num(statistic, 2),
                       sprintf("%s (df = %s)",
                               fmt_num(statistic, 2), fmt_num(df, 1))),
    p        = fmt_p(p_value),
    `Effect size (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s = %s %s",
                                     ifelse(str_detect(es_name, "Cohen"), "d", "r"),
                                     fmt_num(es, 2),
                                     fmt_ci(es_ci_lo, es_ci_hi, 2))
  ) |>
  select(Variable, P_value, SZ_value, Test, Statistic, p,
         `Effect size (95% CI)`)

stim_table_df <- bind_rows(continu_rows, gender_first_row) |>
  rename(!!sprintf("P (n = %d)", n_p) := P_value,
         !!sprintf("SZ (n = %d)", n_sz) := SZ_value)

if (nrow(gender_rows) > 1) {
  for (i in 2:nrow(gender_rows)) {
    stim_table_df <- add_row(
      stim_table_df,
      Variable = paste0("  ", gender_rows$stim_gender[i]),
      !!sprintf("P (n = %d)", n_p)  := gender_rows[[2]][i],
      !!sprintf("SZ (n = %d)", n_sz) := gender_rows[[3]][i],
      Test = "", Statistic = "", p = "", `Effect size (95% CI)` = ""
    )
  }
}

ft_stim <- plos_table(
  stim_table_df,
  title = "Demographic and cognitive characteristics of stimulus participants by group.",
  footnote = c(
    paste0("P, healthy controls; SZ, individuals with a diagnosis of schizophrenia. ",
           "SD, standard deviation; CI, confidence interval; ",
           "d, Cohen's d; V, Cramér's V."),
    paste0("Tests were selected automatically based on Shapiro-Wilk (normality) ",
           "and Levene (variance homogeneity) tests; p-values are two-sided.")
  )
)

4.3 SZ clinical characteristics

Purpose. Describe clinical characteristics of the SZ subgroup.

sz_only <- data_stimuli |> filter(stim_group == "SZ")
vars_sz <- c("stim_PANSS_positive", "stim_PANSS_negative",
             "stim_PANSS_psychopathology",
             "stim_diagnostic_duration", "stim_chlorpro_mg")

sz_descr <- map_dfr(vars_sz, function(v) {
  x <- sz_only[[v]]
  shap <- if (sum(!is.na(x)) >= 3) shapiro.test(x)$p.value else NA_real_
  tibble(
    Variable           = pretty_label(v),
    n                  = sum(!is.na(x)),
    `Mean (SD)`        = fmt_msd(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    `Median [Q1, Q3]`  = fmt_med_iqr(x, 2),
    Range              = sprintf("%s - %s",
                                 fmt_num(suppressWarnings(min(x, na.rm = TRUE)), 1),
                                 fmt_num(suppressWarnings(max(x, na.rm = TRUE)), 1)),
    `Shapiro-Wilk p`   = fmt_p(shap)
  )
})

ft_sz <- plos_table(
  sz_descr,
  title = "Clinical characteristics of the SZ subgroup.",
  footnote = paste0("Q1, first quartile; Q3, third quartile. ",
                    "PANSS, Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale. ",
                    "chlorpro mg = chlorpromazine-equivalent daily dose.")
)

4.5 First impressions: descriptive statistics by group

Purpose. Describe the total first-impression score and each of the ten items by group (P vs. SZ) at the evaluation level (one row per observer × video). These are descriptive only; the inferential group comparison is the linear mixed model in the next section (H1).

imp_targets <- c("imp_total_score", IMPRESSION_ITEMS)

imp_descr <- map_dfr(imp_targets, function(v) {
  d <- data_complete |> filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]))
  by_group <- d |>
    group_by(stim_group) |>
    summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
              m = mean(.data[[v]]),
              s = sd(.data[[v]]),
              med = median(.data[[v]]),
              q1  = quantile(.data[[v]], 0.25),
              q3  = quantile(.data[[v]], 0.75),
              .groups = "drop")
  p_row <- by_group |> filter(stim_group == "P")
  s_row <- by_group |> filter(stim_group == "SZ")
  tibble(
    Variable         = ifelse(v == "imp_total_score",
                              "Total impression score", pretty_label(v)),
    `P n`            = p_row$n,
    `P mean (SD)`    = fmt_msd(p_row$m, p_row$s, 2),
    `P median [IQR]` = sprintf("%s [%s, %s]",
                               fmt_num(p_row$med, 2),
                               fmt_num(p_row$q1, 2), fmt_num(p_row$q3, 2)),
    `SZ n`           = s_row$n,
    `SZ mean (SD)`   = fmt_msd(s_row$m, s_row$s, 2),
    `SZ median [IQR]`= sprintf("%s [%s, %s]",
                               fmt_num(s_row$med, 2),
                               fmt_num(s_row$q1, 2), fmt_num(s_row$q3, 2))
  )
})

ft_imp_descr <- plos_table(
  imp_descr,
  title    = "Descriptive statistics of the first-impression scores by group.",
  footnote = c(
    paste0("Evaluation-level data (one row per observer x video). ",
           "n is the number of evaluations contributing to each group."),
    paste0("Values are descriptive; the group difference is tested with a ",
           "linear mixed model accounting for the observer x video structure ",
           "(see H1).")
  )
)

5 H1 - Does diagnostic group predict first impressions?

5.1 Total score (linear mixed model)

Purpose. Test whether the total first-impression score differs between the SZ and P groups while accounting for the nested structure of the data (each observer rates several videos, each video is rated by several observers).

Variables. Outcome: imp_total_score. Fixed effect: stim_group (reference = P). Random intercepts: observer (obs_id) and video (vid).

m_total <- fit_lmm(data_complete, "imp_total_score", "stim_group")
res_total <- extract_lmm_results(m_total, "stim_group")

# Standardised mean-difference effect size (Cohen's d, SZ - P)
d_total <- lmm_cohens_d(m_total, "stim_group", ref = "P")

# Adjusted means (emmeans) for plotting and reporting
emm_total <- emmeans::emmeans(m_total, ~ stim_group) |>
  as.data.frame() |> normalize_emm_ci()

lmm_total_tab <- tibble(
  Outcome     = "Total impression score",
  Comparison  = "SZ vs. P (P = reference)",
  `β (95% CI)`= sprintf("%s %s",
                        fmt_num(res_total$estimate, 2),
                        fmt_ci(res_total$ci_lo, res_total$ci_hi, 2)),
  SE          = fmt_num(res_total$se, 2),
  df          = fmt_num(res_total$df, 1),
  t           = fmt_num(res_total$statistic, 2),
  p           = fmt_p(res_total$p_value),
  `Cohen's d (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s %s",
                                 fmt_num(d_total$d, 2),
                                 fmt_ci(d_total$d_lo, d_total$d_hi, 2)),
  `R² marginal`    = fmt_num(res_total$r2_marg, 3),
  `R² conditional` = fmt_num(res_total$r2_cond, 3),
  `f²`        = fmt_num(res_total$f2, 3)
)

ft_lmm_total <- plos_table(
  lmm_total_tab,
  title = "Linear mixed model for the total first-impression score (H1).",
  footnote = c(
    paste0("Model: imp_total_score ~ stim_group + (1 | obs_id) + (1 | vid). ",
           "REML estimation; Satterthwaite denominator df."),
    paste0("β, estimated mean difference (SZ - P); CI, confidence interval; ",
           "Cohen's d, adjusted mean difference (SZ - P) standardised by the ",
           "total SD (observer + video + residual); ",
           "R² marginal, variance explained by fixed effects (Nakagawa); ",
           "R² conditional, variance explained by fixed + random effects; ",
           "f² = R²marg / (1 - R²marg)."),
    model_info_line(m_total)
  )
)

5.2 Item-level analyses

Purpose. Examine the effect of group on each of the 10 first-impression items separately. BH-adjusted p-values are reported across the ten items.

items_summary <- run_lmm_set(
  data        = data_complete,
  outcomes    = IMPRESSION_ITEMS,
  fixed_term  = "stim_group",
  target_term = "stim_group",
  bh_correction    = TRUE,
  save_diagnostics = FALSE
)

# Standardised mean-difference effect size (Cohen's d, SZ - P) per item
items_d <- map_dfr(IMPRESSION_ITEMS, function(it) {
  m <- fit_lmm(data_complete, it, "stim_group")
  bind_cols(tibble(outcome = it), lmm_cohens_d(m, "stim_group", ref = "P"))
})
items_summary <- left_join(items_summary, items_d, by = "outcome")

items_tab <- items_summary |>
  mutate(
    Item        = pretty_label(outcome),
    `β (95% CI)`= sprintf("%s %s",

    df          = fmt_num(df, 1),

    `R² marg`   = fmt_num(r2_marg, 3),

  select(Item, `β (95% CI)`, SE, df, t, p, `p (BH)`,
         `Cohen's d (95% CI)`, `R² marg`, `R² cond`, `f²`)

6 Movement features: correlations and aggregation (PCA)

Purpose. Before aggregating, examine how the four directional movement features — quantity of motion (QoM) of the hands and of the head, each in the horizontal and vertical directions — covary across stimuli. Strong inter-correlations justify reducing them to a single composite, used throughout H2-H4. These construction steps are reported as supplementary material (they are not themselves a hypothesis test).

Method. Correlations among the four features at the stimulus level (one value per stimulus). Pearson’s r is used when all features are approximately normal (Shapiro-Wilk p > .05), otherwise Spearman’s ρ. Reporting Pearson when appropriate keeps this step consistent with the PCA, which decomposes the Pearson correlation matrix.

mov_mat <- data_stimuli |>
  select(all_of(MOVEMENT_VARS)) |>
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

# Pearson if all features ~normal, otherwise Spearman
shap_p   <- vapply(mov_mat, function(z) shapiro.test(z)$p.value, numeric(1))
cor_meth <- if (all(shap_p > 0.05)) "pearson" else "spearman"
meth_lab <- if (cor_meth == "pearson") "Pearson" else "Spearman"
coef_sym <- if (cor_meth == "pearson") "r" else "rho"
cmat     <- cor(mov_mat, method = cor_meth, use = "complete.obs")

cor_tab <- as.data.frame(round(cmat, 2)) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Feature") |>
  mutate(Feature = unname(MOVEMENT_LABELS[Feature]))
names(cor_tab)[-1] <- unname(MOVEMENT_LABELS[colnames(cmat)])

ft_mov_cor <- plos_table(
  cor_tab,
  title = sprintf("%s correlations among the four directional movement features.",
                  meth_lab),
  footnote = sprintf(paste0("Stimulus-level analysis (n = %d stimuli with ",
                            "complete movement data). %s coefficient (chosen ",
                            "from Shapiro-Wilk normality of all features). ",
                            "QoM, quantity of motion (rate, per second)."),
                     nrow(mov_mat), meth_lab)
)

6.1 Aggregating the movement features (principal component analysis)

Method. PCA on the four z-standardised features at the stimulus level (psych::principal), reported with sampling-adequacy diagnostics (KMO, Bartlett), eigenvalues, communalities and a scree plot. The dominant component is oriented so that higher = more movement, rescaled to unit SD, and merged onto the evaluation-level data as move_total_pc1.

pca_input <- data_stimuli |>
  select(stim_id, all_of(MOVEMENT_VARS)) |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(MOVEMENT_VARS), ~ !is.na(.)))

X <- pca_input |> select(all_of(MOVEMENT_VARS))
R <- cor(X)

# Sampling adequacy
kmo  <- psych::KMO(R)
bart <- psych::cortest.bartlett(R, n = nrow(X))

# Eigenvalues and number of components
eig <- eigen(R, only.values = TRUE)$values

n_keep <- max(1L, sum(eig > 1))

n_parallel <- tryCatch(
  psych::fa.parallel(
    X,
    fa = "pc",
    plot = FALSE,
    n.iter = 100
  )$ncomp,
  error = function(e) NA_integer_
)
## Parallel analysis suggests that the number of factors =  NA  and the number of components =  1
# Keep the original variable name for compatibility
rot <- "none"

# PCA
pca_move <- psych::principal(
  X,
  nfactors = n_keep,
  rotate = rot,
  scores = TRUE
)

# Dominant component, oriented so higher = more movement
ssl <- colSums(unclass(pca_move$loadings)^2)
main_comp <- names(ssl)[which.max(ssl)]

ld_main <- unclass(pca_move$loadings)[, main_comp]
flip <- if (sum(ld_main) < 0) -1 else 1
score_m <- as.numeric(pca_move$scores[, main_comp]) * flip

# Standardised overall movement score
pca_scores <- tibble::tibble(
  stim_id = pca_input$stim_id,
  move_total_pc1 = as.numeric(scale(score_m))
)

data_complete <- data_complete |>
  left_join(pca_scores, by = "stim_id")

data_stimuli <- data_stimuli |>
  left_join(pca_scores, by = "stim_id")

# Table 1: sampling adequacy
suit_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Statistic = c(
    "KMO (overall MSA)",
    "Bartlett chi-square",
    "Bartlett df",
    "Bartlett p",
    "n (stimuli)"
  ),
  Value = c(
    fmt_num(kmo$MSA, 3),
    fmt_num(bart$chisq, 1),
    as.character(bart$df),
    fmt_p(bart$p.value),
    as.character(nrow(X))
  )
)

ft_suit <- plos_table(
  suit_tab,
  title = "Suitability of the movement features for PCA.",
  footnote = paste0(
    "PCA was based on the Pearson correlation matrix. ",
    "KMO and Bartlett's test are reported as descriptive checks ",
    "of the correlation structure."
  )
)

7 H2 - Does diagnostic group predict overall movement?

Purpose. Describe the four movement features by group and formally test the group difference on the aggregate movement score (overall PCA component) at the stimulus level.

mov_summary <- map_dfr(MOVEMENT_VARS, function(v) {
  d <- data_stimuli |> filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]))
  by_group <- d |>
    group_by(stim_group) |>
    summarise(n = dplyr::n(), m = mean(.data[[v]]), s = sd(.data[[v]]),
              med = median(.data[[v]]), q1 = quantile(.data[[v]], .25),
              q3 = quantile(.data[[v]], .75),
              shap = if (dplyr::n() >= 3) shapiro.test(.data[[v]])$p.value else NA_real_,
              .groups = "drop")
  normal_p <- all(by_group$shap > 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
  p_row <- by_group |> filter(stim_group == "P")
  s_row <- by_group |> filter(stim_group == "SZ")
  tibble(
    Feature      = unname(MOVEMENT_LABELS[v]),
    `P n`        = p_row$n,
    `P summary`  = if (normal_p) fmt_msd(p_row$m, p_row$s, 3)
                   else sprintf("%s [%s, %s]", fmt_num(p_row$med,3), fmt_num(p_row$q1,3), fmt_num(p_row$q3,3)),
    `SZ n`       = s_row$n,
    `SZ summary` = if (normal_p) fmt_msd(s_row$m, s_row$s, 3)
                   else sprintf("%s [%s, %s]", fmt_num(s_row$med,3), fmt_num(s_row$q1,3), fmt_num(s_row$q3,3)),
    Distribution = if (normal_p) "Normal" else "Non-normal"
  )
})
ft_mov_descr <- plos_table(
  mov_summary,
  title    = "Stimulus-level descriptive statistics for the four movement features, by group.",
  footnote = paste0("Mean (SD) for approximately normal variables; median ",
                    "[Q1, Q3] otherwise (Shapiro-Wilk within group, alpha = 0.05). ",
                    "QoM normalised by video duration (rate, per second).")
)

8 H3 - Does overall movement predict first impressions?

Purpose. Test whether overall body movement (the aggregate PCA component) predicts the total first-impression score, with the same observer × video random structure.

Variables. Outcome: imp_total_score. Fixed effect: move_total_pc1 (unit-SD overall movement score). Random intercepts: observer (obs_id) and video (vid).

m_pc1 <- fit_lmm(data_complete, "imp_total_score", "move_total_pc1")

pc1_fixed <- lmm_fixed_table(m_pc1, drop_intercept = TRUE)

r2_pc1  <- tryCatch(performance::r2(m_pc1), error = function(e) NULL)
r2m_pc1 <- if (!is.null(r2_pc1)) as.numeric(r2_pc1$R2_marginal)    else NA_real_
r2c_pc1 <- if (!is.null(r2_pc1)) as.numeric(r2_pc1$R2_conditional) else NA_real_

# Video-level R2: proportion of BETWEEN-VIDEO variance explained by movement
# (Snijders & Bosker level-2 R2: reduction in the video variance vs a model
# without movement). More informative than the marginal R2 for a video-level
# predictor, since the marginal R2 is diluted by observer + residual variance.
vid_var <- function(m) {
  vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(m)); vc$vcov[vc$grp == "vid"]
}
m_null_mov <- fit_lmm(data_complete, "imp_total_score", "1")   # no movement
r2_video   <- 1 - vid_var(m_pc1) / vid_var(m_null_mov)

pc1_lmm_tab <- pc1_fixed |>
  mutate(
    Predictor    = "Overall movement (PCA)",
    `β (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s %s", fmt_num(estimate, 3),
                           fmt_ci(ci_lo, ci_hi, 3)),
    SE           = fmt_num(se, 3),
    df           = fmt_num(df, 1),
    t            = fmt_num(statistic, 2),
    p            = fmt_p(p_value)
  ) |>
  select(Predictor, `β (95% CI)`, SE, df, t, p)

ft_lmm_pc1 <- plos_table(
  pc1_lmm_tab,
  title = "Linear mixed model predicting the total first-impression score from overall movement (PCA component) (H3).",
  footnote = c(
    paste0("Model: imp_total_score ~ move_total_pc1 + (1 | obs_id) + ",
           "(1 | vid). REML; Satterthwaite df."),
    sprintf(paste0("Whole-model effect sizes: marginal R2 = %s (movement), ",
                   "conditional R2 = %s (PC1 + random effects); f2 = %s."),
            fmt_num(r2m_pc1, 3), fmt_num(r2c_pc1, 3),
            fmt_num(if (!is.na(r2m_pc1) && r2m_pc1 < 1) r2m_pc1/(1-r2m_pc1) else NA_real_, 3)),
    sprintf(paste0("Video-level R2 = %s (proportion of between-video variance ",
                   "explained by movement; Snijders & Bosker level-2 R2)."),
            fmt_num(r2_video, 3)),
    paste0("PC1 is standardised to unit SD; β is the change in total ",
           "impression score per 1 SD increase in overall body movement."),
    model_info_line(m_pc1)
  )
)

# Fixed-effect prediction line over the PC1 range
rng_pc1 <- range(data_complete$move_total_pc1, na.rm = TRUE)
x_seq   <- seq(rng_pc1[1], rng_pc1[2], length.out = 100)
newdat  <- tibble::tibble(move_total_pc1 = x_seq)

Xp    <- model.matrix(~ move_total_pc1, newdat)
beta  <- lme4::fixef(m_pc1)
Vp    <- as.matrix(vcov(m_pc1))
predp <- as.numeric(Xp %*% beta)
sep   <- sqrt(diag(Xp %*% Vp %*% t(Xp)))
pred_pc1 <- tibble::tibble(x = x_seq, y = predp,
                           lo = predp - 1.96 * sep, hi = predp + 1.96 * sep)

# Observer-BLUP-adjusted per-video means (purged of observer tendencies)
re_obs_pc1 <- lme4::ranef(m_pc1)$obs_id |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("obs_id") |>
  mutate(obs_id = as.character(obs_id)) |>
  rename(u_obs = `(Intercept)`)

pts_pc1 <- data_complete |>
  mutate(obs_id     = as.character(obs_id),
         stim_group = factor(stim_group, levels = c("P", "SZ"))) |>
  filter(!is.na(move_total_pc1), !is.na(imp_total_score), !is.na(obs_id)) |>
  left_join(re_obs_pc1, by = "obs_id") |>
  mutate(y_adj = imp_total_score - u_obs) |>
  group_by(stim_id, stim_group) |>
  summarise(x = dplyr::first(move_total_pc1),
            imp_adj = mean(y_adj, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

fig_pc1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = pred_pc1, aes(x = x, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              alpha = 0.15, fill = "grey60") +
  geom_line(data = pred_pc1, aes(x = x, y = y),
            linewidth = 0.8, colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data = pts_pc1, aes(x = x, y = imp_adj, fill = stim_group),
             shape = 21, size = 2.6, colour = "black", alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = GROUP_COLOURS,
    name = "Group",
    breaks = c("P", "SZ"),
    labels = c("HC", "IDS")
  ) +
  labs(x = "Overall standardized quantity of motion",
       y = "Observer total first impressions score",
       caption = paste0(
         "Black line: fixed-effect prediction from the PC1 LMM. ",
         "Grey ribbon: 95% CI. Points: observer-adjusted per-video means.\n",
         "HC, healthy controls; IDS, individuals with a diagnosis of schizophrenia.")) +
  theme_plos()

9 H4 - Group and movement jointly

Purpose. This is the first-impressions model of the total score (H1) with aggregate movement added as a second fixed effect. It answers two questions at once: (i) does movement predict impressions after adjusting for diagnostic group, and (ii) does the group difference shrink once movement is taken into account — a mediation-style question (movement as a candidate behavioural pathway for the group difference).

Variables. Outcome: imp_total_score. Fixed effects: stim_group (SZ vs P) and move_total_pc1 (unit-SD aggregate movement). Random intercepts: observer (obs_id) and video (vid).

Caveat. Group and movement are both stimulus-level and correlated (movement discriminates the groups), so they are partially collinear; the individual coefficients are therefore estimated with less precision (VIF reported below), and the attenuation is descriptive, not a formal mediation test.

m_grp_pc1 <- fit_lmm(data_complete, "imp_total_score",
                     "stim_group + move_total_pc1")

gp_fixed <- lmm_fixed_table(m_grp_pc1, drop_intercept = TRUE)

r2_gp  <- tryCatch(performance::r2(m_grp_pc1), error = function(e) NULL)
r2m_gp <- if (!is.null(r2_gp)) as.numeric(r2_gp$R2_marginal)    else NA_real_
r2c_gp <- if (!is.null(r2_gp)) as.numeric(r2_gp$R2_conditional) else NA_real_

label_term <- function(x) dplyr::case_when(
  grepl("move_total_pc1", x) ~ "Overall movement (PCA)",
  grepl("stim_group",     x) ~ "Group (SZ vs P)",
  TRUE ~ x)

gp_tab <- gp_fixed |>
  mutate(
    Predictor    = label_term(term),
    `β (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s %s", fmt_num(estimate, 2),
                           fmt_ci(ci_lo, ci_hi, 2)),
    SE           = fmt_num(se, 2),
    df           = fmt_num(df, 1),
    t            = fmt_num(statistic, 2),
    p            = fmt_p(p_value)
  ) |>
  select(Predictor, `β (95% CI)`, SE, df, t, p)

ft_lmm_gp <- plos_table(
  gp_tab,
  title = "Linear mixed model predicting the total first-impression score from group and overall movement jointly (H4).",
  footnote = c(
    paste0("Model: imp_total_score ~ stim_group + move_total_pc1 + ",
           "(1 | obs_id) + (1 | vid). REML; Satterthwaite df. β for group is ",
           "the SZ - P difference adjusting for movement; β for PC1 is per ",
           "1 SD of movement adjusting for group."),
    sprintf(paste0("Whole-model effect sizes: marginal R2 = %s; ",
                   "conditional R2 = %s; f2 = %s."),
            fmt_num(r2m_gp, 3), fmt_num(r2c_gp, 3),
            fmt_num(if (!is.na(r2m_gp) && r2m_gp < 1) r2m_gp/(1-r2m_gp) else NA_real_, 3)),
    model_info_line(m_grp_pc1)
  )
)

10 Robustness: cluster bootstrap

Purpose. The total-score model and most item models showed mild heteroscedasticity. To verify that the key conclusions do not depend on the residual-variance assumptions, the principal fixed effects of H1, H3 and H4 are re-estimated with a cluster bootstrap: whole stimuli (videos) are resampled with replacement and each model is refitted, giving robust standard errors, percentile 95 % confidence intervals and p-values. Resampling at the stimulus level is appropriate because group and movement vary at that level, and — unlike CR2/sandwich estimators, which require the random effects to be nested within the clustering variable — the bootstrap is valid for the crossed observer × video structure used here. H2 (a simple two-group test, not an LMM) is not part of this bootstrap.

# Bootstrap replicates. 500 is enough for a sensitivity check; raise to
# 1000-2000 for the final run. ~B x 3 model refits, so the FIRST knit takes
# a few minutes (results are cached afterwards).
B_BOOT <- 1000

boot_total   <- cluster_bootstrap_lmm(m_total,   cluster = "vid", B = B_BOOT)
boot_pc1     <- cluster_bootstrap_lmm(m_pc1,     cluster = "vid", B = B_BOOT)
boot_grp_pc1 <- cluster_bootstrap_lmm(m_grp_pc1, cluster = "vid", B = B_BOOT)

rob_specs <- list(
  list(boot = boot_total,   model = m_total,   term = "stim_group",
       label = "Group (SZ - P): total-score model", hyp = "H1"),
  list(boot = boot_pc1,     model = m_pc1,     term = "move_total_pc1",
       label = "Overall movement: movement model", hyp = "H3"),
  list(boot = boot_grp_pc1, model = m_grp_pc1, term = "stim_group",
       label = "Group (SZ - P): group + movement", hyp = "H4"),
  list(boot = boot_grp_pc1, model = m_grp_pc1, term = "move_total_pc1",
       label = "Overall movement: group + movement", hyp = "H4")
)

rob_rows <- map_dfr(rob_specs, function(s) {
  mb <- extract_lmm_results(s$model, s$term)
  rr <- if (!is.null(s$boot)) s$boot[grepl(s$term, s$boot$term), ] else NULL
  has <- !is.null(rr) && nrow(rr) > 0
  tibble::tibble(
    Effect              = s$label,
    hyp                 = s$hyp,
    `β`                 = fmt_num(mb$estimate, 2),
    `Model SE`          = fmt_num(mb$se, 2),
    `Model p`           = fmt_p(mb$p_value),
    `Bootstrap SE`      = if (has) fmt_num(rr$boot_se, 2) else "—",
    `Bootstrap 95% CI`  = if (has) fmt_ci(rr$ci_lo, rr$ci_hi, 2) else "—",
    `Bootstrap p`       = if (has) fmt_p(rr$p_value) else "—"
  )
})

# Number of successful refits (surfaced so failures are visible, not silent)
n_ok <- min(c(boot_total$n_boot, boot_pc1$n_boot, boot_grp_pc1$n_boot),
            na.rm = TRUE)
boot_note <- if (all(vapply(list(boot_total, boot_pc1, boot_grp_pc1),
                            is.null, logical(1)))) {
  paste0("Bootstrap returned no result: the clustering variable 'vid' was ",
         "not found in the model frame. Check the random-effect name.")
} else {
  sprintf("Successful refits per model: at least %d of %d replicates.",
          n_ok, B_BOOT)
}

rob_footnote <- c(
  sprintf(paste0("Non-parametric cluster bootstrap resampling whole video ",
                 "stimuli with replacement (%d replicates); percentile 95%% ",
                 "CIs and two-sided p-values. β is on the raw ",
                 "total-impression-score scale."), B_BOOT),
  paste0("Agreement between the model-based and bootstrap columns indicates ",
         "the conclusions are robust to the residual-variance (homoscedasticity) ",
         "assumption and to the small number of stimuli."),
  boot_note
)

# The combined bootstrap table is split into its three hypothesis-specific
# rows/tables so each lives alongside its model's other results (H1, H3, H4).
ft_robust_h1 <- plos_table(
  rob_rows |> filter(hyp == "H1") |> select(-hyp),
  title    = "Cluster-bootstrap sensitivity analysis for the group effect on total impression score (H1).",
  footnote = rob_footnote
)

11 Supplementary: exploratory correlations (SZ subgroup)

Purpose (exploratory). In the SZ subgroup, examine (a) the association between the movement features and the clinical characteristics, and (b) the association between the clinical characteristics and the total first-impression score. Given the small SZ sample, these analyses are exploratory (post-hoc) and use Spearman’s ρ.

Method. Spearman’s ρ with 95 % CI from Fisher’s z transformation. The movement analysis uses the overall movement score (aggregate PCA component); the clinical × first-impression analysis uses, for each SZ stimulus, the mean total impression score across observers. BH adjustment is applied across the set of clinical variables within each analysis.

clinical_vars <- c("stim_PANSS_negative",
                   "stim_PANSS_positive",
                   "stim_PANSS_psychopathology",
                   "stim_diagnostic_duration",
                   "stim_chlorpro_mg")

11.1 Movement and clinical characteristics

# Re-derive the SZ subset from data_stimuli (it now contains move_total_pc1,
# added by the PCA chunk; sz_only was created earlier, before the PCA).
sz_mov <- data_stimuli |> filter(stim_group == "SZ")

cor_mov_clin <- map_dfr(clinical_vars, function(cv) {
  d <- sz_mov |> filter(!is.na(move_total_pc1), !is.na(.data[[cv]]))
  spearman_with_ci(d$move_total_pc1, d[[cv]]) |>
    mutate(y = cv)
})
cor_mov_clin$p_value_BH <- p.adjust(cor_mov_clin$p_value, method = "BH")

cor_mov_clin_tab <- cor_mov_clin |>
  mutate(
    Clinical     = pretty_label(y),
    `ρ (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s %s", fmt_num(rho, 2), fmt_ci(ci_lo, ci_hi, 2)),
    p            = fmt_p(p_value),
    `p (BH)`     = fmt_p(p_value_BH)
  ) |>
  select(Clinical, n, `ρ (95% CI)`, p, `p (BH)`)

ft_cor_mov_clin <- plos_table(

)

  geom_text(data = ann_mc, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
            hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.4, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            size = 3, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_wrap(~ clinical, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(title   = "Overall movement and clinical variables (SZ subgroup)",
       x       = "Clinical variable",
       y       = "Overall movement (PCA, SD units)",
       caption = paste0(
         "SZ subgroup. Spearman correlations (annotations: rho and BH p). ",
         "Linear fit for visualisation only.")) +
  theme_plos() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 9), axis.text = element_text(size = 8))

11.2 Clinical characteristics and total first-impression score

# Per-stimulus mean total impression score (SZ subgroup)
imp_by_stim <- data_complete |>
  filter(!is.na(imp_total_score)) |>
  group_by(stim_id) |>
  summarise(imp_total_mean = mean(imp_total_score), .groups = "drop")

sz_clin_imp <- sz_only |>
  left_join(imp_by_stim, by = "stim_id")

cor_clin_imp <- spearman_multi(
  sz_clin_imp, y = "imp_total_mean", xs = clinical_vars,
  bh_correction = TRUE
)

cor_clin_imp_tab <- cor_clin_imp |>
  mutate(
    Clinical     = pretty_label(x),
    n            = n,
    `ρ (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s %s", fmt_num(rho, 2), fmt_ci(ci_lo, ci_hi, 2)),
    p            = fmt_p(p_value),
    `p (BH)`     = fmt_p(p_value_BH)
  ) |>
  select(Clinical, n, `ρ (95% CI)`, p, `p (BH)`)

ft_cor_clin_imp <- plos_table(
  cor_clin_imp_tab,
  title    = "Exploratory Spearman correlations between clinical variables and the total first-impression score (SZ subgroup).",
  footnote = c(
    paste0("SZ subgroup only. The first-impression score is the per-stimulus ",
           "mean of the total impression score across observers. ",
           "95% confidence intervals from Fisher's z transformation."),
    paste0("p (BH): Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value across the clinical ",
           "variables. Exploratory.")
  )
)

  select(all_of(clinical_vars), imp_total_mean) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(clinical_vars), names_to = "clinical", values_to = "cv") |>
  mutate(clinical = pretty_label(clinical))

ann_ci <- cor_clin_imp |>
  mutate(clinical = pretty_label(x),
         label    = sprintf("rho = %s, %s",
                            fmt_num(rho, 2),
                            ifelse(fmt_p(p_value_BH) == "<.001",
                                   "p (BH) <.001",
                                   paste0("p (BH) = ", fmt_p(p_value_BH)))))

fig_cor_ci <- ggplot(scatter_ci, aes(x = cv, y = imp_total_mean)) +
  geom_point(colour = GROUP_COLOURS["SZ"], alpha = 0.85, size = 1.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "grey20",
              fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0.6) +

            hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.4, inherit.aes = FALSE,

12 Discussion notes

This notebook produces the descriptive and inferential outputs for the corresponding manuscript, organised by hypothesis under results/: descriptive/ (purely descriptive tables), H1/ through H4/ (one folder per hypothesis, each with its tables, figures, diagnostics and bootstrap sensitivity check), and supplementary/ (scale reliability, the movement PCA construction, and exploratory/symptom correlations). Tables are exported as Word .docx (cell-based) and figures as TIFF (300 dpi) and PNG (inline viewing).

Every linear mixed model reports both the marginal/conditional R² and an explicit partition of the random variance (variance components, proportion of residual variance, ICC), so that the share of information captured by the observer and video random effects is visible.

The interpretation of effect sizes, clinical implications, and limitations should be developed in the manuscript itself.

13 Supporting information

S1 Table. Cronbach’s α if each item is dropped. Internal-consistency diagnostic of the first-impression scale. See results/supplementary/table_S1_cronbach_if_dropped.docx.

S2 Table. Diagnostic checks for the total first-impression-score LMM (H1). Residual normality (Shapiro–Wilk), homoscedasticity (Breusch–Pagan-type auxiliary regression), random-effect normality (Shapiro–Wilk on the BLUPs of obs_id and vid), singular-fit and convergence flags. See results/H1/table_S2_lmm_total_diagnostics.docx.

S3 Table. Diagnostic checks for the 10 item-level LMMs (H1). As S2, per item.

S4 Table. Diagnostic checks for the overall-movement impression LMM (H3). As S2, for the model using the overall movement score (aggregate PCA component) as a single fixed effect. See results/H3/table_S4_lmm_movement_diagnostics.docx.

S5 Table. Diagnostic checks for the group + movement first-impression LMM (H4). As S2, for the model with diagnostic group and overall movement entered jointly. See results/H4/table_S5_lmm_group_movement_diagnostics.docx.

S1 Figure. Scree plot of the movement-feature PCA. Eigenvalues of the components with the Kaiser reference line (eigenvalue = 1). File: results/supplementary/FigS1_pca_scree.{tiff,png}.

S Figures. Diagnostic plots from performance::check_model(). Residual, QQ, posterior-predictive and random-effect diagnostic panels for each LMM. Files: results/H1/diag_lmm_*.png, results/H3/diag_lmm_*.png, results/H4/diag_lmm_*.png.

S1 File. Processed long data set. data/questionnaire_and_merged/02_data_complete.csv — one row per observer × video evaluation.

S2 File. Stimulus-level data set. data/questionnaire_and_merged/02_data_stimuli.csv — one row per stimulus.

S3 File. Observer-level data set. data/questionnaire_and_merged/02_data_observers.csv — one row per observer.

S4 File. PC1-augmented data sets. results/supplementary/data_complete_with_movement_pc1.csv and results/supplementary/data_stimuli_with_movement_pc1.csv — the same tables with the aggregate movement score (move_total_pc1) added.
